Numbers, terms and formulas

A price with 19% VAT, the formula for kinetic energy, a temperature of −7 °C: before we start with functions, we brush up the tools of the trade. You sort numbers into number sets, read the structure of a term, rearrange formulas and calculate confidently with percentages and powers.

6 LESSONS3 UNITS2 LABSBASICS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • assign numbers to the sets $\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ and calculate with the absolute value
  • recognise the structure of a term and apply the binomial formulas forwards and backwards
  • rearrange formulas for any quantity
  • calculate confidently with percentages, growth factors and powers

UNIT 12 LESSONS

1Number sets and absolute value

A thermometer shows −7 °C, €0.35 interest lands in the account, and the diagonal of a square tile with 1 m sides is $\sqrt{2}\,\text{m} \approx 1.414\,\text{m}$ long. None of these numbers is a natural number.

Number sets were always extended when a calculation was impossible in the old set: $3 - 5$ has no solution in $\mathbb{N}$, so we need the negative numbers. $3 : 4$ is impossible in $\mathbb{Z}$, so we need fractions. And $x^2 = 2$ has no solution in $\mathbb{Q}$: for that we need the irrational numbers.

KEY POINT · NUMBER SETS AND ABSOLUTE VALUE

$\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$ natural numbers · $\mathbb{Z} = \{\ldots, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, \ldots\}$ integers

$\mathbb{Q}$ rational numbers: all fractions $\tfrac{p}{q}$ with $p \in \mathbb{Z}$, $q \in \mathbb{N}$, $q \neq 0$. As a decimal terminating or recurring.

$\mathbb{R}$ real numbers: in addition the irrational numbers, neither terminating nor recurring, such as $\sqrt{2}$ or $\pi$.

$\mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R}$ · notation: $3 \in \mathbb{N}$, $-3 \notin \mathbb{N}$

Absolute value: $|a| = a$ for $a \geq 0$ and $|a| = -a$ for $a < 0$. It is the distance of the number from $0$ on the number line, so it is never negative.

With or without zero? According to the German standard DIN 5473, $0$ belongs to $\mathbb{N}$. Without zero one writes $\mathbb{N}^*$ or $\mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$.

Set symbols: $A \cup B$ is the union, $A \cap B$ the intersection, $A \setminus B$ means “$A$ without $B$”. Example: $\mathbb{Z} \setminus \mathbb{N} = \{-1, -2, -3, \ldots\}$.

Distance: $|x - 2|$ is the distance of the number $x$ from the number $2$.

INTERACTIVE · WHERE DOES THE NUMBER BELONG?

Every number belongs to the smallest set it lies in. If necessary, work it out first.

EXAMPLE 1 · SORTING NUMBERS

What is the smallest number set containing $-5$, $\tfrac27$, $\sqrt{16}$, $\sqrt{7}$ and $0.\overline{12}$?

$-5 \in \mathbb{Z}$ · $\tfrac27 = 0.\overline{285714} \in \mathbb{Q}$ · $\sqrt{16} = 4 \in \mathbb{N}$ · $\sqrt{7}$ is irrational, so $\in \mathbb{R}$.

$0.\overline{12}$: with $x = 0.1212\ldots$ we get $100x = 12.1212\ldots$, so $99x = 12$ and $x = \tfrac{12}{99} = \tfrac{4}{33} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

EXAMPLE 2 · CALCULATING WITH THE ABSOLUTE VALUE

Calculate $|-4.5|$ and $|3 - 8|$. Solve $|x - 2| = 5$.

$|-4.5| = 4.5$ and $|3 - 8| = |-5| = 5$.

$|x - 2| = 5$ means: $x$ is 5 away from the number 2. So $x - 2 = 5$ or $x - 2 = -5$: $x = 7$ or $x = -3$.

EXERCISES

True or false? a) $-2 \in \mathbb{N}$   b) $0.75 \in \mathbb{Q}$   c) $\sqrt{9} \in \mathbb{Z}$   d) $\pi \in \mathbb{Q}$   e) $\mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Q}$

a) false   b) true ($\tfrac34$)   c) true ($\sqrt{9} = 3$)   d) false, $\pi$ is irrational   e) true

Calculate: a) $|-12|$   b) $|7 - 10|$   c) $-|-3|$   d) $|-2| \cdot |5|$

a) $12$   b) $3$   c) $-3$   d) $10$

Write as a fraction: a) $0.4$   b) $0.\overline{3}$   c) $1.25$   d) $0.\overline{7}$

For d): $x = 0.777\ldots$, then $10x = 7.777\ldots$ Subtract one equation from the other.

a) $\tfrac25$   b) $\tfrac13$   c) $\tfrac54$   d) $9x = 7$, so $\tfrac79$

Solve: a) $|x| = 6$   b) $|x - 1| = 4$   c) $|x + 3| = 0$   d) $|x| = -2$

a) $x = 6$ or $x = -6$   b) $x = 5$ or $x = -3$   c) $x = -3$   d) no solution, an absolute value is never negative

Show that between two different rational numbers there is always another rational number. So how many lie between them?

For $a < b$ the mean $\tfrac{a + b}{2}$ lies between the two, and it is a fraction again. Between $a$ and the mean there is another one, and so on: infinitely many.

TEST YOURSELF!

Which number is irrational?

$\sqrt{49} = 7$ and $0.\overline{5} = \tfrac59$ are rational. $50$ is not a square number, so $\sqrt{50}$ is irrational.

Calculate $|-3 - 5|$.

$|-8| = 8$

What is the negative solution of $|x - 1| = 8$?

$x - 1 = -8$, so $x = -7$ (the other solution is $9$).

UNIT 22 LESSONS

2Terms, binomial formulas and rearranging formulas

A trapezium has the area $A = \tfrac{a + c}{2} \cdot h$. We are looking for the height of a trapezium with $A = 30\,\text{cm}^2$, $a = 7\,\text{cm}$ and $c = 5\,\text{cm}$. Instead of trying again every time, we rearrange the formula for $h$ once: $h = \tfrac{2A}{a + c} = \tfrac{60}{12} = 5\,\text{cm}$.

The structure of a term is determined by the operation carried out last: $\tfrac{a + c}{2} \cdot h$ is a product, $3x^2 - 5$ a difference, $\tfrac{x + 1}{x - 2}$ a quotient. This matters, because you may only cancel factors, and when rearranging you undo the operation carried out last first.

KEY POINT · BINOMIAL FORMULAS AND REARRANGING

$(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$ · $(a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2$ · $(a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2$

Rearranging formulas: do the same thing to both sides (equivalence transformation). Undo the operations in reverse order: whatever happened last to the quantity you are looking for is undone first.

Cancel only in products: $\tfrac{2x + 4}{2} = \tfrac{2(x + 2)}{2} = x + 2$. But $\tfrac{x + 4}{2}$ cannot be cancelled.

Backwards: $x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2$ and $49 - y^2 = (7 - y)(7 + y)$.

INTERACTIVE · THE FIRST BINOMIAL FORMULA AS AN AREA

The big square has side $a + b$. It consists of two squares and two equal rectangles.

EXAMPLE 3 · SIMPLIFYING CLEVERLY

Simplify $(2x + 3)^2 - (2x - 3)^2$.

Multiplied out: $(4x^2 + 12x + 9) - (4x^2 - 12x + 9) = 24x$.

Faster with the third binomial formula, $A = 2x + 3$, $B = 2x - 3$: $(A + B)(A - B) = 4x \cdot 6 =$ $24x$.

EXAMPLE 4 · REARRANGING A FORMULA

The kinetic energy is $E = \tfrac12\,m\,v^2$. Rearrange for $v$. How fast is a car with $m = 1500\,\text{kg}$ and $E = 300\,000\,\text{J}$?

$E = \tfrac12 m v^2 \;\big|\; \cdot 2 \;\Rightarrow\; 2E = m v^2 \;\big|\; : m \;\Rightarrow\; v^2 = \tfrac{2E}{m} \;\Rightarrow\; v = \sqrt{\tfrac{2E}{m}}$ (speed positive).

$v = \sqrt{\tfrac{600\,000}{1500}} = \sqrt{400} = $ $20\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}} = 72\,\tfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}$

EXERCISES

What is the structure of the term? a) $3(x + 2)$   b) $3x + 2$   c) $(x - 1)^2$   d) $\tfrac{x}{2} - 1$

a) product   b) sum   c) power, i.e. a product $(x - 1)(x - 1)$   d) difference

Multiply out: a) $(x + 5)^2$   b) $(3 - 2y)^2$   c) $(4a + 1)(4a - 1)$

a) $x^2 + 10x + 25$   b) $9 - 12y + 4y^2$   c) $16a^2 - 1$

Write as a product: a) $x^2 + 8x + 16$   b) $25 - 10z + z^2$   c) $9x^2 - 4$

a) $(x + 4)^2$   b) $(5 - z)^2$   c) $(3x - 2)(3x + 2)$

Rearrange: a) $U = 2(a + b)$ for $b$   b) $A = \tfrac12\,g\,h$ for $h$   c) $F = m \cdot a$ for $m$   d) $K = K_0 + K_0 \cdot \tfrac{p}{100}$ for $K_0$

For d), first factor out $K_0$: $K = K_0 \left(1 + \tfrac{p}{100}\right)$.

a) $b = \tfrac{U}{2} - a$   b) $h = \tfrac{2A}{g}$   c) $m = \tfrac{F}{a}$   d) $K_0 = \dfrac{K}{1 + \frac{p}{100}}$

Work out in your head with a binomial formula: a) $102^2$   b) $49 \cdot 51$   c) $999^2$

a) $(100 + 2)^2 = 10\,404$   b) $(50 - 1)(50 + 1) = 2500 - 1 = 2499$   c) $(1000 - 1)^2 = 1\,000\,000 - 2000 + 1 = 998\,001$

TEST YOURSELF!

We have $(x + 6)^2 = x^2 + bx + 36$. What is $b$?

$2 \cdot 6 = 12$

A trapezium has $A = 30\,\text{cm}^2$, $a = 7\,\text{cm}$ and $c = 5\,\text{cm}$. How high is it?

$h = \tfrac{2A}{a + c} = \tfrac{60}{12} = 5$ cm

Which rearrangement of $A = \tfrac12\,g\,h$ for $g$ is correct?

Times 2, then divided by $h$: $g = \tfrac{2A}{h}$.

UNIT 32 LESSONS

3Percentages and powers

A bicycle costs €800 net. With 19% VAT it costs $800 \cdot 1.19 = 952$ euros. In the clearance sale there is a 20% discount on this price: $952 \cdot 0.8 = 761.60$ euros. Instead of working out percentages one by one, you multiply by a factor.

If a quantity increases several times in a row by the same percentage, you multiply several times by the same factor. This is how powers arise: three years of 3% interest mean the factor $1.03 \cdot 1.03 \cdot 1.03 = 1.03^3 \approx 1.0927$, i.e. just under 9.3% more and not 9%.

KEY POINT · PERCENTAGES AND LAWS OF INDICES

Percentage amount $W = G \cdot \tfrac{p}{100}$ · increased base value $G \cdot \left(1 + \tfrac{p}{100}\right)$ · decreased base value $G \cdot \left(1 - \tfrac{p}{100}\right)$. Several changes: multiply the factors.

$a^m \cdot a^n = a^{m + n}$ · $a^m : a^n = a^{m - n}$ · $(a^m)^n = a^{m \cdot n}$ · $a^n \cdot b^n = (ab)^n$ · $a^n : b^n = \left(\tfrac{a}{b}\right)^n$

$a^0 = 1$ · $a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}$ · $a^{\frac1n} = \sqrt[n]{a}$ and $a^{\frac{m}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a^m}$ (for $a > 0$)

Percentage points: if an interest rate rises from 4% to 5%, that is 1 percentage point more, but 25% more interest.

Powers of ten: $3 \cdot 10^{-6}\,\text{m} = 0.000\,003\,\text{m}$, that is roughly the size of a bacterium.

POWERS LABPowers and roots as graphs
INTERACTIVE · PLUS 3% AGAIN AND AGAIN

Simple interest grows by the same amount every year; with compound interest you multiply by the same factor every year.

EXAMPLE 5 · FROM GROSS TO NET

A mobile phone costs €595 including 19% VAT. What are the net price and the tax?

Gross = net $\cdot 1.19$, so net $= 595 : 1.19 = $ €500. The tax is $595 - 500 = 95$ euros.

Careful: 19% of €595 would be €113.05. The percentage refers to the net price.

EXAMPLE 6 · LAWS OF INDICES

Simplify a) $\dfrac{a^3 \cdot a^{-5}}{a^{-4}}$   b) $8^{\frac23}$   c) $(2 \cdot 10^3) \cdot (4 \cdot 10^{-5})$

a) $a^{3 - 5 - (-4)} = $ $a^2$   b) $\left(\sqrt[3]{8}\right)^2 = 2^2 = $ $4$

c) $8 \cdot 10^{3 - 5} = 8 \cdot 10^{-2} = $ $0.08$

EXERCISES

a) What is 15% of €240?   b) What percentage of €160 is €24?   c) 12% is 18 kg. What is the base value?

a) €36   b) $\tfrac{24}{160} = 0.15 = 15\%$   c) $18 : 0.12 = 150$ kg

Calculate: a) $2^3 \cdot 2^4$   b) $5^7 : 5^5$   c) $(3^2)^3$   d) $10^{-3}$   e) $16^{\frac12}$

a) $2^7 = 128$   b) $5^2 = 25$   c) $3^6 = 729$   d) $0.001$   e) $\sqrt{16} = 4$

A price rises twice in a row by 10%. By what percentage has it risen altogether?

$1.1 \cdot 1.1 = 1.21$, so by 21%, not by 20%.

Simplify: a) $x^5 \cdot x^{-2}$   b) $(2a^3)^2$   c) $\dfrac{(x^2 y)^3}{x\,y^2}$   d) $27^{\frac23}$

a) $x^3$   b) $4a^6$   c) $\dfrac{x^6 y^3}{x\,y^2} = x^5 y$   d) $\left(\sqrt[3]{27}\right)^2 = 9$

A share loses 50% and then gains 50%. “Then it is back where it was,” someone says. Is that right? By what percentage would it have to rise after the loss?

$0.5 \cdot 1.5 = 0.75$: it stands 25% below the old level. Getting from half back to the whole takes a doubling, i.e. 100%.

TEST YOURSELF!

How much does €800 net cost with 19% VAT?

$800 \cdot 1.19 = 952$ euros

A price rises by 20% and then falls by 20%. By what percentage is it below the starting price?

$1.2 \cdot 0.8 = 0.96$, so 4% below.

Calculate $2^{-3}$.

$\tfrac{1}{2^3} = \tfrac18 = 0.125$

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Put in order of size: $\sqrt{10}$, $3.14$, $\pi$, $\tfrac{22}{7}$, $3.\overline{1}$

$3.\overline{1} < 3.14 < \pi < \tfrac{22}{7} < \sqrt{10}$   ($3.111\ldots$, $3.14$, $3.14159\ldots$, $3.142857\ldots$, $3.1623\ldots$)

An invoice shows €47.50 VAT (19%). What are the net and gross amounts?

Net: $47.50 : 0.19 = 250$ euros · gross: $250 + 47.50 = 297.50$ euros

Rearrange the formula for the volume of a sphere $V = \tfrac43\,\pi\,r^3$ for $r$. What is the radius of a sphere with a volume of 1 litre $= 1000\,\text{cm}^3$?

$r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3V}{4\pi}} = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3000}{4\pi}} \approx \sqrt[3]{238.7} \approx$ $6.2\,\text{cm}$

Show: $(a + b)^2 - (a - b)^2 = 4ab$. Use it to calculate $4 \cdot 17 \cdot 3$ as the difference of two square numbers.

$(a^2 + 2ab + b^2) - (a^2 - 2ab + b^2) = 4ab$. With $a = 17$, $b = 3$: $20^2 - 14^2 = 400 - 196 = 204$.

EXCURSIONA PROOF FROM ANTIQUITY

Why $\sqrt{2}$ is not a fraction

For a long time the Greeks believed that any two line segments can be measured with a common unit, i.e. that every ratio of lengths is a fraction. The diagonal of a square does not fit this picture. The proof is a proof by contradiction:

Suppose $\sqrt{2} = \tfrac{p}{q}$ with a fully simplified fraction. Then $p^2 = 2q^2$, so $p^2$ is even and therefore so is $p$. With $p = 2r$ it follows that $4r^2 = 2q^2$, i.e. $q^2 = 2r^2$. Then $q$ is even too. Numerator and denominator would both be divisible by 2, so the fraction would not be fully simplified after all. The assumption was wrong: $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.

Source: Aristotle mentions this proof as an example of a proof by contradiction: if the diagonal were commensurable with the side, an odd number would equal an even one. Aristotle, “Prior Analytics” I, 23, 41a26–27.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

NUMBER SETS

$\mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R}$. Rational means: terminating or recurring. Irrational: neither.

$-3 \in \mathbb{Z}$ · $0.\overline{3} = \tfrac13 \in \mathbb{Q}$ · $\sqrt{2} \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}$

ABSOLUTE VALUE

$|a|$ is the distance from $0$, never negative. $|x - b|$ is the distance from $b$.

$|x - 2| = 5$: $x = 7$ or $x = -3$

BINOMIAL FORMULAS

$(a \pm b)^2 = a^2 \pm 2ab + b^2$ · $(a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2$

$9x^2 - 4 = (3x - 2)(3x + 2)$

REARRANGING FORMULAS

Do the same thing to both sides, undo the operations in reverse order.

$E = \tfrac12 m v^2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\tfrac{2E}{m}}$

PERCENTAGES

$W = G \cdot \tfrac{p}{100}$. Changes as factors $1 \pm \tfrac{p}{100}$, for several changes multiply.

$+20\%$, then $-20\%$: $1.2 \cdot 0.8 = 0.96$

POWERS

$a^m a^n = a^{m+n}$ · $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$ · $a^{-n} = \tfrac{1}{a^n}$ · $a^{\frac{m}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a^m}$

$8^{\frac23} = 4$ · $2^{-3} = \tfrac18$
